answer.reason: I set up the full 252-state d5 problem, including electron repulsion (B = 800 cm⁻¹, C/B = 4.341) and an octahedral field, then solved it at each Dq/B and identified each term by its spin and symmetry. In units of B: at Dq/B = 1.45 the ground term is 6A1g and the three lowest excited terms are 4T1g (20.456), 2T2g (25.002) and 4T2g (26.246); at 2.55 the ground term is still 6A1g and they are 2T2g (4.106), 4T1g (9.798) and 4T2g (16.777); by 3.25 the ion has gone low-spin, the ground term is 2T2g, and the three lowest excited terms measured from it are 6A1g (9.449), 4T1g (12.369) and 4T2g (19.637). As a check, the zero-field energies match the free-ion values (4G at 10B + 5C and 4P at 7B + 7C).

def g(a,b,c,d): # <ab|1/r|cd>, a,c electron1

    return h

D=len(dets)

    pass

    st2=tuple(sorted(st+(o,))); i=st2.index(o); return (-1)**i, st2

    s1,st=r; r=cre(i,st)
    if r is None: return None

        s,st=r; r=ann(d,st)

        s*=r[0]; st=r[1]; r=cre(b,st)
        if r is None: continue
        s*=r[0]; st=r[1]; r=cre(a,st)

def h1mat(h):

                r=one(i,j,det)

        ch=np.real(np.trace(vs.conj().T@np.diag(C4)@vs))/mult
        out.append((round((w[i]-w[0])/B,3),f"{mult}{names.get((sp,int(round(ch))),'?')}"))
        i=j
    print(x,out[:5])
